findings.topic: The previous discrete encoding branch has a measured negative economy result
findings.finding: Cycle96 preserves all source ordinals/predictions but produces 19,555,087 raw bytes versus 7,848,960, 8,062,001 gzip bytes versus 7,139,604, and a 15,640,256-byte index. Almost all COPY runs are length one. The fixed codec is not a reason to continue grammar/domain search.
findings.limit: This total order includes mutually exclusive token identities at a key position. The result does not exclude a smaller legal-history comparator or other symbolic attention representation.

findings.topic: Exact selection leaves an actual coefficient dependency
findings.finding: Cycle97 retains 477 dependent padding queries, 426 changed ordered supports and 428 nonzero read changes. The two unchanged-support nonzero cases change both allocation and payload. Allocation/read-change norm 0.909508 and payload/read-change norm 0.404401 are vector ratios, not causal percentages. There are 145 negative row cross terms but positive pooled cross. The scalar conditional-weight premise holds to approximately 1.67e-16 and B reconstruction to 2.78e-16 only with supplied b.
findings.limit: No new coefficient or value producer is established by the ratio identities; scalar summaries are source-reported/additive-public evidence, not a new independent vector replay in this survey.

findings.topic: Cycle98 gives an implementable partial-evaluation boundary and a scaling warning
findings.finding: A fixed padding-query/head token/absolute-position score function has 3,924,480 FP64 entries, 31,395,840 bytes and 502,333,440 paid offline coordinate products in the current domain. The old rank bundle does not contain magnitudes. Ideal relative-position symmetry is not universally exact under separately rounded BF16 rotary operations; the supplied rational example is not a native measurement.
findings.limit: Literal full-key-vocabulary/32-head storage is 5,088,168,902,656 bytes; all query IDs give 773,076,030,393,942,016 strict-past bytes plus a legal same-token diagonal. These are neither information lower bounds nor measured compression results. Direct weighted Fourier/phase recurrence still pays learned arithmetic unless further lowered.

findings.topic: The strongest nearby state evidence supports dependency completeness, not another generic dense compression campaign
findings.finding: Restoring native predecessor states changes four-digit first-token agreement 364/2048 to 2019/2048; restoring the equals state alone gives 367. Native assistance remains paid, and alternate-prefix/finite-layout exceptions remain. Whole-stack gate/up factors remove 40.895% nominal linear MACs but answer 0/8 versus native7/8, even while own-state refresh improves source geometry and local writes. Value changes can pass through the same initial attention allocation before native MLPs form different later queries.
findings.limit: These findings identify missing current/contextual carriers and expose local-versus-future mismatch. They do not prove all compact states or economical transitions impossible, or identify a new nonneural contextual initializer.

findings.topic: Foretelling supplies executable conditional relations, not free operands
findings.finding: The source uses original linear maps, native history, RMS/SwiGLU/attention and JVP formation. Second-order weight forecasts improve7/8 receivers but one worsens versus stale; consumer success remains mixed and source coefficients/native state cost work. A scalar final evaluator does not remove that formation cost.
findings.limit: Useful future-consumer localization and coefficient reuse are retained. No general raw-prompt-to-state/pixel program follows from them.

findings.topic: Actual discrete and program-discovery achievements have supplied domains
findings.finding: ISA serves a learned finite Boolean response table with eight supplied 64-bit registers, flags and bounded raw windows; it has useful own-state continuation and retained exceptions, not a raw-language initializer. Math/e-graph work extracts exact cheaper expressions but starts with supplied algebraic features/rules/search problems and often retains a neural scorer. Specialist unions and strong local fidelity can worsen the actual consumer.
findings.limit: These are constructive examples of source-qualified program families. They do not supply the FLUX context, denoising or pixel family required here. No new handwritten parser/renderer is licensed by this analogy.

findings.topic: Architecture and proof tools remain useful but do not replace scientific construction
findings.finding: Typed state, dependency bindings, native-consumer tests, exact partial evaluation, program execution and bounded own-state continuations are implemented in inspected scopes. General economical contextual resolving, arbitrary-prompt semantic initialization, reusable own-state image evolution and a general nonneural pixel readout remain unestablished in those scopes.
findings.limit: No broad absence or global impossibility claim. Lack of an exact global proof is not a discovery gate; a concrete source-bound exploratory candidate may still be tested with costs and provenance explicit.

decision.status: Retain one bounded compiled-selected-mass construction question for the next cycle; cycle99 closes as research/storage review only.
decision.selectedQuestion: Can the fixed source score function S(i,u,j), composed with the existing own-history integer selector, form all selected weights for covered new histories without online Q/K products, old weights, edited-address mass b, or per-history answer lookup?
decision.rationale: This changes a supplied dependency into an input-defined producer. It is the smallest concrete missing edge identified by cycle97, and the source-defined compiler is available. No newly inventoried/read source provides a stronger ready contextual-state/pixel construction that should replace it. The result is a reusable source/serving separation within one finite primitive, not a general scaling strategy.
decision.fixedScope: Head0, pad151643, 30 discovery key IDs, L512, strict-past positions, original95 score contract and selector. One declared CPU assay only after a separate source/resource review; A/B plus one predeclared controlled in-domain history pair and explicit unknown-ID refusal. No fit, rank/seed/codec sweep, vocabulary/head expansion, V mixing, suffix, new reference image or image continuation.
decision.finiteContract: Recompile exact qualified BF16 rotary operands into scaled FP64 individual coordinate products and pinned math.fsum; compare all old score hashes if reused. Store LE FP64 S and independently bind score/rank domains. Fresh stdlib serving forms its own legal support, retrieves up to4 scores, then executes the explicitly new max/subtract/math.exp/math.fsum/division order. Empty/short histories, selected order, tied scores, underflow and unsupported histories must remain explicit. This is not universal finite parity with historical NumPy normalization.
decision.sourceServingSeparation: No Q/K vectors, checkpoints, learned products, old selected weights or b in the fresh serving process. Offline learned work, asset provenance, tokenizer/local-atom formation and all remaining scalar attention arithmetic are paid. Removing framework/model calls alone is not a zero-neural claim.
decision.accounting: Charge 502,333,440 compile products and3,924,480 reductions, rotary/scaling, serialization/hash/load bytes, 31,395,840 uncompressed score bytes plus7,848,960 rank bytes and runtime/index overhead. Charge rank selection/history, up-to4 score lookups/exponentials, max/subtractions/sum/divisions. Direct source references after serving seal are diagnostic work, separately counted. Reusing the same score helper is a same-profile direct reference, not an independent arithmetic implementation.
decision.terminalClaimLimit: At most a source-qualified bounded selected-mass producer with no online QK products. Scalar attention still runs; full reader/value formation, contextual continuation, raw-prompt coverage, own denoising and pixel decoding remain unresolved. Exactness/storage/runtime are observations within their declared mechanics/consumer scope, not arbitrary quality gates.
decision.alternatives: Ideal Fourier/clock recurrence is not selected because it still computes learned weighted scores and lacks the source finite contract. A new dense factorization or further Hankel toy panel would not address this missing producer edge. Direct deeper-context/pixel program discovery remains the stronger long-term route, but the inspected evidence does not yet specify an executable family to test without inventing semantics.
decision.afterThisCut: Close this finite coefficient-port question, regardless of favorable or unfavorable economy; do not default to scaling the cache or tuning its format. Reassess the earliest contextual boundary where token-local operand identity ceases to be sufficient. A stronger source-derived update/readout family with an actual initializer, bounded retained state and a consumer would supersede the cache lane. No further assay is authorized by this recommendation alone.
